lectures.title: New species and biodiversity: blood group, species projects, CMS COP15

parts.t: JAMA: the 49th human blood group system
items: **Recognition:** JAMA was recognised on September 14, 2026 as the 49th human blood group system.
**Recognised by:** International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT); ISBT number 049.
**Discovery:** joint investigation by researchers from the United Kingdom and Israel.
**Samples:** scientists investigated unusual blood samples from an Israeli woman and her brother.
**Antibody:** the woman's blood contained an antibody that reacted with red blood cells of most people.
**No reaction:** this reaction did not occur with her own red blood cells or those of her brother.
**New antigen:** the antibody did not correspond to any previously identified blood group antigen; the investigation led to the identification of the JAMA blood group system.
**Antigen:** found on the red blood cells of most people; it was absent in the woman and her brother, whose blood contained the corresponding antibody.
**Significance:** the discovery is significant for transfusion medicine.
**Examiner's trap:** JAMA is not another blood type alongside A, B, AB and O. It is a separate blood group system involving a specific antigen.

parts.t: Ganges soft-shell turtle: first satellite tagging
items: **Event:** India's first satellite-tagged Ganges soft-shell turtle was released on May 15, 2026.
**Location:** Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, Assam; area 1,302 sq. km.
**Status:** it is an endangered species, listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
**Soft-shell turtles:** eight species of soft-shell turtles are reported from India; five are known from the Kaziranga landscape.
**Distinctive feature:** it can be distinguished by distinctive arrowhead-shaped markings on the top of its head.

parts.t: Project Great Indian Bustard: new chicks and breeding
items: **Date of update:** June 14, 2026. **Species:** Great Indian Bustard (Godawan), Ardeotis nigriceps. **Location:** Rajasthan.
**New chicks:** three additional chicks were reported in the conservation breeding programme.
**Fourth year of captive breeding:** total chicks hatched reached 26; captive stock increased to 94 birds.
**Break-up of the 26:** 18 chicks through artificial insemination, four through natural breeding and four from wild-collected eggs.
**In the wild:** three chicks also hatched in the wild in Rajasthan through a jumpstart intervention involving wild eggs.
**Status:** Critically Endangered species; flagship grassland bird; indicator of healthy grassland ecosystems; Rajasthan's State Bird.
**First state:** Rajasthan was the first state to launch a dedicated conservation project for the species.
**Launch:** Project Great Indian Bustard was launched on June 5, 2013; initially implemented in Desert National Park, Jaisalmer.

parts.t: CMS COP15: 40 species receive new or upgraded protection
items: **Event:** 15th Conference of Parties to the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS COP15).
**Dates and venue:** March 23–29, 2026, Campo Grande, Brazil.
**Major outcome:** 40 species, subspecies and populations received new or upgraded treaty protection; they were included in or upgraded under CMS Appendices I and II.
**Types covered:** birds, aquatic wildlife, terrestrial animals.
**Current coverage:** the Convention now covers more than 1,200 unique species.
**Bonn Convention:** CMS is also known as the Bonn Convention; it was signed in 1979 in Bonn.
**Presidency:** Brazil holds the CMS COP Presidency for three years following COP15.
**Next COP:** COP16, Bonn, Germany, 2029; the 2029 meeting will coincide with the 50th anniversary of CMS.
**Important distinction:** these are species receiving upgraded conservation protection, not necessarily newly discovered species.

parts.t: National repositories: Bhavasagara and Natural History Museum
items: Bhavasagara – National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna
**Location:** Centre for Marine Living Resources & Ecology (CMLRE), Kochi, Kerala.
**Designation:** National Repository for Deep-Sea Fauna, designated by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
**CMLRE:** functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
**Role:** specialised national facility dedicated to deep-sea biodiversity; repository for deep-sea faunal collections from India's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
**Collection:** maintains more than 3,560 taxonomically identified and geo-referenced voucher specimens; supports capacity building in deep-sea taxonomy.
**Institution:** Natural History Museum (NHM), Mizoram University, Aizawl, Mizoram.
**Designation:** India's 21st Designated Repository, under Section 39 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
**Designating ministry:** Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
**Achievement:** on September 4, 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) validated Bhutan's elimination of dog-transmitted human rabies as a public-health problem.
**Bhutan** became the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to achieve this milestone.
**Record:** zero human deaths from dog-mediated rabies since June 2023.
**Validated countries:** WHO listed Bhutan, Chile and Mexico as countries validated for this form of elimination.
**Validation criteria:** at least two years without dog-mediated rabies deaths and the capacity to prevent re-emergence.
**Rabies:** a viral disease; it is almost always fatal after clinical symptoms appear.
**PEP:** timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) can prevent deaths; it involves wound washing, rabies vaccination and rabies immunoglobulins when indicated.
**Transmission:** infected dogs account for up to 99% of human rabies transmissions globally.

lectures.title: New Acts and Rules of 2026: VB-G RAM G, Vande Mataram, plastic waste

parts.t: VB-G RAM G Act: background and employment guarantee
items: **Name:** Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-G RAM G Act).
**Replaces:** the Act was replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 (MGNREGA), described as repealed and replaced by it.
**Launch:** the new Act was launched across rural India on 1 July 2026.
**What it does:** guarantees wage employment and links employment with productive public assets, transparency, convergence, climate resilience and local economic development.
**Associated phrase:** “Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi” – employment with dignity.
**Employment guarantee** increased from 100 to 125 days per financial year for rural households whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
**Wage floor:** notified minimum wage floor for 2026–27: ₹300 per day.
**Payment of wages:** wages should be paid weekly or within 15 days of work and muster-roll closure.
**Delayed compensation:** 0.05% of unpaid wages per day beyond the 16th day after closure.

parts.t: VB-G RAM G Act: job cards, allowance, priorities, funding
items: **Job cards:** existing e-KYC-verified job cards remain valid until Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Cards are issued; pending e-KYC cannot justify denial of employment.
**Registration and demand:** workers may register at Gram Panchayats; work may be demanded orally, through Form-6 or digitally.
**Entitlement:** failure to provide employment within the prescribed timeframe entitles workers to unemployment allowance.
**Rate:** at least one-fourth of the notified wage for the first 30 days of the financial year; one-half of the notified wage for the remaining period.
**Priority areas:** 1. Water security. 2. Rural infrastructure. 3. Livelihood infrastructure. 4. Climate resilience.
**Mother Sanction:** more than ₹25,000 crore was released as the first installment, called the Mother Sanction.
**Investment:** total ₹7.5 lakh crore, as of July 2026, to be invested in 2.86 lakh Panchayats over five years.
**Total outlay:** including the estimated State share, the total outlay is expected to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore.

parts.t: Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026
items: Cleared the Bill before the Lok Sabha vote
The amendment makes intentional disruption or prevention of the singing of the national song **Vande Mataram** a criminal offence.
**Same protection:** grants Vande Mataram the same legal protection as the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana; the amendment extends legal enforceability to Vande Mataram.
**1971 Act:** the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 was enacted to prevent insults to national honour; it covers insults to the National Flag and the Constitution of India.
**Section 3:** intentionally preventing the singing of the National Anthem or disturbing an assembly engaged in such singing is punishable with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both.
**Composer:** Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
**Publication:** first published in Bangadarshan in 1875; later included in Anandamath in 1882.
**Music:** set to music by Rabindranath Tagore; sung by Rabindranath Tagore at the INC session of 1896.
**Notified:** by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 31 March 2026.
**Nature:** further amends the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016; does not replace the 2016 Rules.
**End-of-Life Disposal:** definition expanded to include energy recovery methods such as co-processing, waste-to-energy, waste-to-oil and road construction.
**Recycling:** processes converting plastic into feedstock or new plastic are classified strictly as recycling, not disposal.
**Plastic Waste Processors:** definition broadened to include recyclers and end-of-life disposal entities.
**New terms introduced:** Registered Environment Auditor, Reuse, Seller.
**Local governance:** scope widened to include all relevant authorities beyond traditional local bodies.
**Standard:** all recycled plastic packaging must comply with Indian Standard IS 14534:2023.
**Labelling:** packaging must carry mandatory labelling indicating recycled content.

parts.t: Kuno: the births of 5 October 2026 and the population
items: **Latest development – 5 October 2026:** five healthy cheetah cubs were born at Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh.
**Announcement:** made by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav.
**Mother:** KJP21, a 32-month-old Indian-born female; she became the third Indian-born female cheetah to give birth, after Mukhi and KGP12.
**Father:** the father was brought from Botswana.
**Population:** the birth increased India's cheetah population to 60, including 41 Indian-born individuals and 19 animals foreign-born.

**In the wild:** three chicks hatched in the wild in Rajasthan through a jumpstart intervention.
